title: Micro-econ workbook: hosted API regional & model snapshots
description: Compact spreadsheet to compare per-token COGS across representative models and regions, plus short action list. Designed as a quick sim for trade-offs between batching, quantization, and reserved capacity for Hosted API pricing decisions.
content:
Overview:
This workbook synthesizes micro-econ inputs into a concise hosted-API per-token COGS view. It is intentionally not the canonical long-form model (see linked Confluence) — it is a lightweight decision support spreadsheet used in product/ops trade-off conversations.

Methodology summary:
- Per-token COGS = GPU runtime cost + network egress + amortized storage & infra + ops overhead.
- GPU runtime cost computed as gpu_ms_per_token * gpu_cost_per_ms. gpu_cost_per_ms is region-specific and depends on VM type and reserved vs on-demand pricing.
- Quantization effect modeled as a multiplicative speedup (quantization_delta) and a possible quality penalty flag (qual_check_needed).
- We include two operational overlays: 1) prefix/KV cache hit rate (reduces effective tokens), 2) batching benefit curve (ms/token drops nonlinearly with batch size).

Representative rows (snapshot numbers used for quick tradeoffs):
- redwood-mix-8B | us-west | seq_len_p50: 64 | gpu_ms_per_token: 1.8 | gpu_cost_per_ms: $0.000011 | gpu_cost_per_token: $0.0000198 | network_cost_per_token: $0.000003 | storage_amort_per_token: $0.000002 | ops_overhead_per_token: $0.000004 | quantization_delta: 0.75 | total_cogs_per_token: $0.000022 | list_price_per_token: $0.00012 | implied_margin: 81.7%
- llama2-70b-q8 | eu-west | seq_len_p50: 80 | gpu_ms_per_token: 4.6 | gpu_cost_per_ms: $0.000015 | gpu_cost_per_token: $0.000069 | network_cost_per_token: $0.000004 | storage_amort_per_token: $0.000006 | ops_overhead_per_token: $0.000006 | quantization_delta: 0.60 | total_cogs_per_token: $0.000046 | list_price_per_token: $0.00018 | implied_margin: 74.4%
- gpt-legacy-13b | ap-south | seq_len_p50: 48 | gpu_ms_per_token: 2.7 | gpu_cost_per_ms: $0.000009 | gpu_cost_per_token: $0.0000243 | network_cost_per_token: $0.000008 | storage_amort_per_token: $0.000003 | ops_overhead_per_token: $0.000005 | quantization_delta: 0.85 | total_cogs_per_token: $0.000036 | list_price_per_token: $0.00010 | implied_margin: 64.0%

Sensitivity experiments included as separate tabs:
- Batch size curve: simulated ms/token vs batch [1,4,8,16,32,64] with tail latency constraints (p95 SLO).
- Cache hit rate sweep: effective tokens reduced by prefix cache hits of [0,10,25,50,75%] to see marginal improvement to unit margin.
- Reserved capacity scenarios: 0% / 30% / 60% reserved; reserved reduces gpu_cost_per_ms by region-specific discount and adds amortized committed cost line.

Key observations from the current snapshot:
1) High-throughput models (large-batch compatible) show the biggest unit-econ improvements from batching and reserved discounts; mid-sized models used for chat/assistant workloads benefit more from prefix caching.
2) APAC regions have materially higher network/ops overlays per token in our assumptions; selecting smaller but quantized model variants for APAC reduces blended COGS more than shifting traffic to US/EU in the short term.
3) Quantization yields a favorable marginal saving, but we flag quality risk for certain prompts. Quantization adoption should be gated by evals per critical prompt set.

Recommendation summary (short action items):
- Short term (30 days):
  * Owner: Marco Alvarez (infra) — run a focused reserved-capacity pilot for redwood-mix-8B in us-west (target 30% commit). Deliver: observed gpu_cost_per_ms delta and expected amortization plan. Due: 2026-03-01.
  * Owner: Liang Chen (applied-ml) — build a 3-prompt quality smoke-test harness for q4 quantized candidates; flag any >2% degradation. Due: 2026-02-25.
  * Owner: Product Optimize (Priya) — adopt a per-region list price floor that preserves >=55% gross margin on a 30% reserved mix; small pricing tweak to ap-south suggested in this sheet. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Medium term (90 days):
  * Owner: DevExp (Samantha) & Solutions Eng — implement better routing policy prototypes to prefer quantized model variants in APAC with automatic rollback on quality regression. Deliverable: routing policy PR + telemetry. Due: 2026-05-15.
  * Owner: Finance (Omar) — provide monthly amortization schedule templates reflecting committed vs burst capacity for Dedicated conversions; add to the workbook as a separate tab. Due: 2026-04-20.

Notes & open questions (work-in-progress):
- Need clearer measurement of p95 / p99 tail penalty from batching in real traffic; our curve uses a synthetic interpolation from serving-runtime experiments (see linked PR).
- Ops overhead attribution (SRE/Support) currently uses a blunt per-token uplift; would like SRE to propose a more granular cost pool (alerts, incident MTTR, on-call).
- Consider adding a customer-segment fold to the sheet (PLG freemium vs enterprise committed) to show blended margin per segment.

Quick usage tips for the sheet:
- Toggle reserved% input on the Assumptions tab to immediately see corrected gpu_cost_per_ms across regions.
- Use the sensitivity scan to find the break-even list price when switching a model to q4 quantized variant.
- The Actionable levers tab provides checkboxes for 'safe to roll' / 'needs-eval' for each model-region cell — use those to gate rollout PRs.

Provenance: compiled by product-optimize from infra cost exports (billing.csv snapshot 2026-01), bench runs (runtimes/bench-2025-11), and initial quality evals (applied-ml/quant-evals Q4 2025).

If you want a condensed one-pager derived from this workbook for exec review, I can produce a 1-slide summary with the 3 most impactful levers and expected 90-day margin lift (quick estimate: 6–10pp uplift if we pursue reserved + batching + targeted quantization in APAC).
